methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective comparative study of 185 adrenal patients (95 LRA, 90 PRA) from single center 2018-2023. Appropriate statistical methods: Student's t-tests, Mann-Whitney U, chi-square/Fisher's exact, propensity score matching (1:1 PSM) to balance confounders. However, surgical approach selection not randomized but determined by surgeon discretion/experience. PSM excluded bilateral cases reducing sample. No pre-specified power calculation reported. Missing data not addressed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective comparative cohort study (LoE 3b) addressing clinically important question of surgical approach selection for minimally invasive adrenalectomy. Direct relevance to operative efficiency and patient outcomes. However, findings are purely comparative without establishing long-term prognostic significance or disease-modifying effects. Applicable to surgical technique optimization but not treatment efficacy per se.

reporting_quality.justification: Adequate STROBE reporting of baseline characteristics, surgical procedures, and outcomes. Methods clearly described with trocar placement and operative techniques detailed. However, significant limitations: no data availability statement; no code/analysis plan preregistration; single-surgeon variability not quantified; operative time definitions potentially variable between surgeons.

novelty_literature.justification: Retrospective comparison of LRA vs PRA approaches; existing literature already reports both techniques effective. Authors cite only two prior direct comparisons (Oh et al., Agha et al.). Main novel finding: PRA reduces operative time by ~23 minutes and hospitalization by ~1.4 days, but both approaches known to be feasible. Incremental confirmation rather than new discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear organization with logical flow from introduction through discussion. Methods adequately detailed regarding surgical techniques with helpful figure illustrations (trocar positioning). Results presented systematically with appropriate tables. Discussion contextualizes findings within broader literature and acknowledges limitations including single-surgeon experience, lack of large tumor cases, and unknown generalizability.

key_strengths: Largest comparative analysis to date (n=185) directly comparing LRA and PRA approaches with appropriate statistical methods
Clear clinical conclusion: PRA offers reduced operative time (56 vs 79 min) and hospitalization (4.5 vs 5.9 days) with equivalent safety profiles
Propensity score matching employed to reduce selection bias; baseline characteristics well-balanced after PSM
Detailed description of surgical techniques with operative views; helpful for training and technique standardization
key_concerns: Single-surgeon or limited surgeon experience severely limits generalizability; learning curves and technique variation unknown
No randomized allocation; surgeon choice of approach based on judgment, not protocol; residual confounding likely
Underrepresentation of large/complex tumors (only 14.6% ≥4cm); findings may not apply to challenging cases where LRA advantages claimed
Retrospective design with no external validation; outcomes may be institution-specific
No discussion of long-term oncologic outcomes (if applicable); study focuses only on operative metrics, not recurrence or survival
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 4 manuscript: competent surgical comparison with clear practical findings but limited novelty and generalizability. Single-center, surgeon-dependent experience. Appropriate for lower-tier surgical journal.
